pr.title: Fix staleness filter for NO variance strategy

report.summary: This PR reworks the market staleness filter in src/gimmes/strategy/staleness.py so a market is only considered stale when price is unchanged AND volume is below a new `volume_floor` AND open interest is unchanged, replacing the previous `volume_spike_ratio` heuristic. It also adds `open_interest` to `StalenessEntry`, updates `ScannerConfig` help text and a CLI comment, and adds five unit tests. Reviewers should focus on the new activity predicate: the volume test now runs against the resolved `volume` value (which falls back to lifetime cumulative volume) and the OI comparison defaults missing data to 0, both of which change which markets get filtered.

suggestions.title: Volume floor is compared against cumulative fallback volume, so dead markets are never filtered
suggestions.reason: The new predicate `has_volume = volume >= volume_floor` (line 79) operates on `volume`, which is resolved on the unchanged line `volume = m.volume_24h if m.volume_24h > 0 else m.volume`. When a market has no trading in the last 24h, `m.volume_24h == 0` and `volume` falls back to the lifetime cumulative `m.volume`, which is above the default floor of 10 for essentially any market that ever traded. As a result `has_volume` is True and the count resets, so the staleness filter can no longer detect markets whose current activity has stopped — the exact case it exists to catch. The new tests never cover this path because `_market` sets `volume_24h=volume`, so the fallback branch is unexercised.
suggestions.recommendation: Base the activity check on recent volume only, or treat the cumulative fallback as not active. For example: `has_volume = m.volume_24h >= volume_floor` (keeping `volume` for storage), or if the fallback must be retained, only apply the floor to it when 24h data is genuinely unavailable and use a much higher threshold. Add a test where `volume_24h=0` and total `volume` is large to lock in the intended behavior.
suggestions.failure_scenario: A market's last trade was several days ago: `m.volume_24h == 0` but `m.volume == 5000`. The fallback resolves `volume` to 5000, `has_volume` is True, `new_count` resets to 0 every scan, and the market is never added to `skipped` even though price is frozen and nothing is trading — the stale market silently passes through the filter indefinitely.
